chapter: Strings, arrangements and the Shrine band
title: The union's string rule of about 1916-17
summary: DeDroit recalls the union rule requiring a string player for every five men, and that he took up fiddle to collect the money.

story.theme_name: The musicians' union: cards, locals, and the Black-white merger
story.community_name: The musicians' union: cards, scale and the black-white merger

blocks.x: Wasn't it so that the union for several years was requesting that you had

at least one ball? I'm going to tell you about that. The union, but that was early. That was early. Let's see. About 1916 or 1917 they had a rule that you must have one string with every five men. So I took up the fiddle. And my father played the trumpet and I played the fiddle. Now you know you can't hire me. No matter who you are, you couldn't hear that fiddle, but I was getting that five bucks or whatever it was. That was the rule. You had to have so many strings. But the string men did that because they weren't not getting any weight.
Before they had been pretty much the thing in the orchestra for dancing.
